title: Attack combination
subtitle: Build a readable attack combination with a reachable response and a useful recovery.
summary: Two or more familiar attacks are sequenced so the first response changes the starting conditions for the next.
overview: Two or more familiar attacks are sequenced so the first response changes the starting conditions for the next, creating a composite decision.
learning: Tune the signal, commitment, geometry, response, and recovery of a attack combination as one rule.

steps.title: Can the player read the complete rule?
steps.body: Preserve the tells of each component and add a rhythm or stance that communicates whether the sequence will continue.

steps.title: Is the intended response reachable?
steps.body: The player chooses a first answer that also leaves space, resources, and facing for the known follow-up rather than solving each hit in isolation.

steps.title: Does recovery create a useful outcome?
steps.body: After the final component, the boss enters a recovery proportional to the combined coverage instead of chaining immediately into a fresh sequence.

mistakes.title: Combining individually fair attacks can still create an unavoidable follow-up if the first recovery ends in the second danger zone
mistakes.body: Combining individually fair attacks can still create an unavoidable follow-up if the first recovery ends in the second danger zone.

mistakes.title: The cue and active geometry disagree
mistakes.body: If the visible attack combination cue promises a different area or timing, the player cannot carry the learned rule into the next cycle.

designNotes.title: Tune the complete rule
designNotes.body: Tune transition gaps, positional carryover, cancellation rules, and total sequence duration; test every legal response to the opening move.

designNotes.title: Escalate one variable at a time
designNotes.body: Branch the final move from a small set of clearly signaled options after the fixed opening sequence is learned.

designNotes.title: Prove the recovery
designNotes.body: After the final component, the boss enters a recovery proportional to the combined coverage instead of chaining immediately into a fresh sequence.

story.title: What the mechanic communicates
story.body: Two or more familiar attacks are sequenced so the first response changes the starting conditions for the next, creating a composite decision. The encounter uses that rule as a short promise: a visible signal, a committed action, and a result the player can verify.

adaptation.title: Adapt it to the player verbs
adaptation.body: The player chooses a first answer that also leaves space, resources, and facing for the known follow-up rather than solving each hit in isolation. Tune transition gaps, positional carryover, cancellation rules, and total sequence duration; test every legal response to the opening move.

distinction.title: Keep the mechanic distinct
distinction.body: Combining individually fair attacks can still create an unavoidable follow-up if the first recovery ends in the second danger zone. Do not hide that distinction behind extra effects or tracking that the announced rule does not contain.

lensNotes.body: The signal must reveal the relevant timing and geometry before commitment.
After commitment, the rule stops changing in ways the signal did not announce.
Preparation, action, and recovery create a legible cycle of pressure and release.
The response uses an ordinary supported verb and produces an observable result.
